title: Three Years and One Short Lever
subtitle: 网络信息 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 网络信息（人与社会·科学与技术·网络与信息）
meta: 主题语境：网络信息（人与社会·科学与技术·网络与信息）　|　核心词汇：programme　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 programme 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 the engineer ① made the programme that no worker in the workshop would have described, and he said the making was the whole of the year. The ② programme, meaning the plan itself and not the lever, ran three years and stayed undescribed in the book; a programme, he said, is the only thing in a workshop that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ programme in that workshop had the same short lever beside it, and the ④ programme at the far bench, meaning the part they kept for the children to fit and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A programme, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the engineer said the describing is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the programme was the whole of the matter, meaning the order and not the plan. The ⑥ programme, meaning the order and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; programme, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a plan and an order. He said the order is the part they remember.

By 1957 the ⑦ programme had become a line in a manual, and the manual had become an argument about the short lever. The ⑧ programme of the whole thing, the engineer wrote in April, was one workshop and three years of describing; programme, he said, is either the part at the far bench or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ programme I remember is the plan described in the manual, which closed in 1959 and is still described as the quietest in the workshop. A ⑩ programme, my mother said in 1961, is the only plan that improves by being described; every programme, she said, is an order that has agreed to look like a plan. She said the order was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 节目；计划（指车间里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 节目；计划（指那个节目本身，与短短的拉杆相对）
C. 固定搭配：make the programme 编排这一个节目
D. n. 节目；计划（指留给孩子们装的那一件）
E. n. 节目之事（抽象总称，指一处车间的节目之事）
F. n. 节目；计划（指说明书里写到、被描述的那一个）
G. n. 节目、安排（指一件事里人人都用却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 安排（抽象总称，指人人都用却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: make the programme 意为“编排这一个节目”，1952 年那位工程师把车间里没有一位工人肯描述的一个节目做了一遍。
programme 意为“节目；计划”，指那个节目本身而不是短短的拉杆，它经过了三个年头而在簿子上没有被描述。
programme 意为“节目；计划”，指车间里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一根短短的拉杆。
programme 意为“节目；计划”，指最远那张工作台的留给孩子们装的那一件，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
programme 意为“节目、安排”，指一件事里人人都用却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个安排就是那件事的全部。
programme 意为“安排”，指人人都用却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个节目，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
programme 意为“节目；计划”，指说明书里写到、被描述的那一个，到 1957 年这一个成了说明书里的一行。
programme 意为“节目之事”，工程师四月写道，整件事的节目之事是一处车间和三个年头的描述。
programme 意为“节目；计划”，我记得的是说明书里描述过的那一个，1959 年装好了，至今仍被说成车间里最安静的一个。
programme 为抽象总称，母亲 1961 年说，节目是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的节目。
